It sounds incredibly exhausting to keep up with such boundless energy, and it is completely understandable that you are looking for ways to help him burn it off so your family can get some rest. You aren't "wrong" for wanting him to have a healthy physical outlet and a reasonable bedtime; parenting a high-energy child is a very real challenge, and you are just trying to find a balance that works for everyone. 

However, since he isn't enjoying traditional team sports like basketball, it might be worth exploring other active outlets that align better with his unique rhythm. Activities like martial arts, swimming, indoor rock climbing, or even unstructured play at a trampoline park might feel less like a chore to him while still giving you that much-needed quiet evening. If his energy levels are consistently impacting his sleep and daily life, it could also be helpful to mention this to his pediatrician, who might have additional strategies to help his body wind down at night.
